title: Distinct Distances in General Position: n/2 Lower Bound

problemStatement.formal: Let A ⊂ ℝ² be a set of n points with no three on a line. Does A determine at least ⌊n/2⌋ distinct distances?
problemStatement.plain: Prove that n points in general position (no three collinear) in the plane determine at least n/2 distinct pairwise distances.
whyMatters: Strengthens Szemerédi's n/3 bound for general position sets
Connected to the Erdős distinct distances problem and Guth-Katz theorem

proven: no_four_equidistant: 4 mutually equidistant points impossible in ℝ² (Lagrange identity proof)
equidistant_system_inconsistent: algebraic core showing d⁴/4 = 3d⁴/4 contradiction
at_least_one_distance: n ≥ 2 points have ≥ 1 distinct distance
conjecture_n_le_3: n/2 conjecture holds for n ≤ 3
at_least_two_distances: Finset of size ≥ 4 has ≥ 2 distinct squared distances
conjecture_n_le_5: n/2 conjecture for all n ≤ 5 (unified theorem)
distSq properties: nonneg, comm, eq_zero_iff, pos_of_ne
open: n/2 conjecture for all n (Erdős Problem 1082, question 1)
knownResults.goal: Formalization complete for provable cases. n/2 verified for n ≤ 5. Main conjecture remains OPEN.

currentState.focus: Extended n/2 conjecture from n ≤ 3 to n ≤ 5 using Finset extraction and pigeonhole on distances
blockers: Main conjecture is OPEN for all n - no known proof exists
currentState.nextAction: No further provable work. n ≥ 6 would require genuinely new combinatorial arguments beyond equidistant point impossibility.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Erdos1082OQ01.lean has 0 sorries, 0 axioms, 12 theorems. Proved n/2 conjecture for n ≤ 5 by connecting no_four_equidistant structural result to Finset distance counting via pigeonhole.
insights: Lagrange identity proof: given u=b-a, v=c-a, δ=e-c all with |·|²=d, perpendicular bisector conditions give δ·u=0, δ·v=-d/2, u·v=d/2
Squaring: (δ×u)²(u×v)² = d²·3d²/4 = 3d⁴/4 but also = (d²/2)² = d⁴/4, so d=0
Working with ℝ×ℝ avoids EuclideanSpace/WithLp abstraction that causes nlinarith issues
Separating algebraic core (equidistant_system_inconsistent) from geometric wrapper (no_four_equidistant) avoids heartbeat limits
Finset extraction via repeated erase: card_pos.mp + card_erase_of_mem + ne_of_mem_erase pattern
Finset.card_eq_one.mp + singleton membership check bridges between card=1 and all-equal
The n/2 bound for n ≤ 5 is tight: 3 equidistant points give only 1 distinct distance, matching ⌊3/2⌋ = 1
nextSteps: No further provable work without breakthrough on the OPEN conjecture
n ≥ 6 requires showing not just ≥ 2 distances but ≥ 3, which needs new combinatorial geometry

approaches.name: Lagrange identity / perpendicular bisector
approaches.description: Use overdetermined perpendicular bisector system in 2D to show 4 equidistant points impossible, then derive small cases of n/2 conjecture

approaches.name: Finset extraction + pigeonhole
approaches.description: Extract 4 distinct points from Finset of size ≥ 4, show singleton distance set contradicts no_four_equidistant, derive ≥ 2 distances

papers: Erdős: 'On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry' (1975)
